Oral and maxillofacial surgery · published research

Buccal fat removal (bichectomy)

A six-case series reported less pain and edema, while a 20-person randomized trial found similar pain and edema with PBM and dexamethasone. Chewing comfort favored PBM on one quality-of-life measure.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

A six-case series reported less pain and edema, while a 20-person randomized trial found similar pain and edema with PBM and dexamethasone. Chewing comfort favored PBM on one quality-of-life measure.

Summary of the Evidence

Two clinical publications directly address postoperative bichectomy or buccal fat-pad removal. A third, separately mapped in-vitro study examines buccal fat-pad stem cells but does not study surgery or postoperative recovery. Other broad surgical records in the source query are not treated as direct evidence for this indication. The two clinical reports are from Brazil; no overlapping cohort is indicated. Da Silva et al. 2020

Human and clinical evidence

The 2018 case series included six cases, three treated and three controls, and reported reduced edema and pain after PBM sessions immediately after surgery and at 24 and 48 hours. The 2020 randomized clinical trial included 20 patients and compared PBM with dexamethasone. It found no difference between groups in pain or edema. One quality-of-life measure, comfort while chewing, favored PBM. The sample was small, and the reports do not establish a large or durable recovery benefit. Bernal Rodriguez et al. 2018

Animal evidence

No animal study directly examining PBM after bichectomy was identified.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

A 2024 study exposed buccal fat-pad stem cells to 980 nm light and reported increased proliferation and osteogenic markers under tested conditions.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The case series used 660 nm intraoral and extraoral treatments over three postoperative sessions. The randomized study record specifies 660 nm treatment at 100 mW and 2 J/cm² per point, with three sessions over five days. The cell study used 980 nm light and a different biological target.

Interpretation

Direct clinical evidence is sparse and mixed. The randomized comparison found similar pain and edema outcomes to dexamethasone, while a chewing-comfort measure favored PBM. The separate cell experiment should not increase confidence in surgical outcomes. Larger controlled trials are needed.

Evidence strength in source summaryPostoperative pain and edema: Mixed small clinical evidence Masticatory comfort: One secondary-outcome signal Stem-cell findings: Laboratory only
Publications and records2 direct human publications: 1 six-case series with 3 treated cases and 3 controls, and 1 randomized trial with 20 participants comparing PBM with dexamethasone.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Two direct clinical publications address bichectomy or buccal fat-pad removal: a six-case series and a 20-person randomized comparison with dexamethasone. Pain and edema were similar between randomized groups, with a difference only in chewing comfort. A separate stem-cell experiment is indirect evidence.

Publication and study types

  • A separate 2024 in-vitro buccal fat-pad stem-cell study is mapped as adjacent laboratory evidence, not a surgical cohort.
  • The two clinical reports are distinct publications; cohort overlap is not indicated.
